newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks driven up by brewer and bank.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks driven up by brewer and bank.

text.p: Colombian stocks drifted up slightly for the second consecutive session as investors moved to snap up shares in brewing giant Bavaria and Banco de Colombia.

Bogota's IBB index ended 0.04 percent higher at 872.89 on a one billion pesos trading volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 0.08 percent to close at 13,671.77 on the back of a 572.8 million peso trade.
"The market was pretty sluggish, but there was still foreign fund demand for Bavaria. I don't think that trend will be maintained," a Bogota broker said.

He said the previous day's demand for Banco de Bogota shares had died down, leading it to close unchanged at 6,100 on a total trade of 22.4 million pesos. The main movers on the Bogota exchange were Banco de Colombia, up 0.24 percent to 416 on a total volume of 507.16 million and Bavaria, up 0.36 percent to 4,085 on a 422.4 million peso volume.

"We saw some cross deals between existing shareholders in Banco de Colombia, which doesn't reflect genuine demand. However, a lot of expectations are riding on this bank's results and on those of other leading companies at the end of this month," the broker added.

In Medellin, the bulk of the day's trading was made up by a 326.7 million cross deal in engineering company Distral, which leapt eight percent to 5,940. Chocolate manufacturer Compania Nacional de Chocolates, lost 0.58 percent to 8,350.1 on a 66.74 million peso trade.

Medellin's general price index was driven up by demand for Bavaria shares, up 0.98 percent, to 4,100 on a 64 million peso volume and in Banco Industrial Colombiano, up 0.28 percent to 3,510 on a 47.2 million peso total trade.
